title: L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 : “Ça m’a vraiment déçue !” Pourquoi Justine a très mal vécu son speed-dating ?
author: Drifa Maza
body:
L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 : “Ça m’a vraiment déçue !” Pourquoi Justine a très mal vécu son speed-dating ?
Publié le Par Drifa Maza
Ce lundi 14 septembre 2026, Justine sera au cœur de l’intrigue amoureuse dans L’Amour est dans le pré, diffusée sur M6. Toutefois, la candidate n’a pas exactement vécu l’aventure à laquelle elle s’attendait. Pourquoi l’étape du speed dating a-t-elle été compliquée pour elle ? Elle s’est confiée sur ses péripéties, plusieurs mois après le tournage.
Depuis plusieurs semaines maintenant, les bandes-annonces de L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 teasent l’épisode sur Justine à travers des extraits montrant notamment l’épreuve du speed dating. Ce lundi 14 septembre, le quatrième épisode, déjà disponible sur M6+, arrive donc enfin à la télévision, pour le plus grand bonheur des téléspectateurs. Et le moins que l’on puisse dire est que l’émission réserve bien des surprises, autant aux agriculteurs qu’aux fidèles du programme.
Dans l’épisode 4 de la saison 21 de L’Amour est dans le pré, diffusé ce lundi soir dès 21 h 10 sur M6, Justine doit faire face à de nombreuses complications qui ont forcément impacté son aventure.
Sommaire
L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 : le rendez-vous de Justine et Audran a viré au cauchemar…
Les spectateurs remarqueront que lors de son rendez-vous avec Audran, Justine n’est pas restée très immobile. En effet, à plusieurs reprises, la trentenaire a quitté le bateau pour prendre l’air. La raison ? Justine a le mal de mer. Malgré les précautions prises par la production, l’étape de la péniche était obligatoire pour le speed dating. Ainsi, l’agricultrice a dû faire face à ses peurs, mais cela n’a pas duré longtemps.
Interrogée par Télé Star sur cette expérience, Justine a déclaré qu’elle n’a malheureusement pas réussi à surmonter cette épreuve : « J’avais prévenu la production, mais j’ai pensé qu’en étant sur une péniche, à quai, sur la Seine, ça irait. Mais ça a été chaotique. Ça a tangué dans tous les sens, dans mon corps et dans ma tête. Les émotions étaient décuplées et je n’étais pas moi-même. Je lui ai fait vivre le pire date de toute sa vie« .
Voilà donc qui vient instantanément expliquer son comportement particulier envers Audran. Mais ce n’est pas tout ! Justine a également dû faire face à un désistement de dernière minute, qu’elle a encore du mal à digérer aujourd’hui…
Pourquoi Clément s’est désisté dans L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 ?
Alors que Justine s’apprêtait à annoncer à Audran et Clément qu’ils ont été choisis pour l’accompagner à la ferme, le prétendant de 24 ans et éducateur sportif, décide de prendre la main sur la situation en lui annonçant qu’il ne souhaite plus continuer l’émission à ses côtés. « C’était juste pour te dire que je ne vais pas donner suite malheureusement. Je n’ai pas eu ce petit coup de cœur même si tu es une nana magnifique. Je préfère stopper là et ne pas te donner de faux espoirs« , lui a alors annoncé Clément en face-à-face.
Toujours au micro de Télé Star, Justine n’a pas hésité à revenir sur cette trahison : « Ça m’a vraiment déçue. Pour moi, j’étais l’objet d’un pari avec ses copains, et j’ai trouvé ça dénigrant. » Justine était, en effet, tombée sous le charme de Clément, mais l’attirance n’était donc pas réciproque. À voir maintenant ce que l’avenir lui réserve au sein du jeu.
Suis-nous sur Google pour ne rien rater de nos quiz et actus séries
Drifa Maza
Journaliste
Journaliste chez Serieously depuis 2023, Drifa Maza est une grande passionnée de cinéma de toutes les époques, allant de ses débuts silencieux en noir et blanc à aujourd’hui. Toujours à l’affut de l’actualité, elle ne rate aucune sortie ciné et série, et est toujours à la recherche d’une nouveauté et d’un show à binger. Son enfance a été bercée par les films Pixar et l’ère Disney Channel, son adolescence par le genre de la dystopie et les Marvel (qu’elle aime toujours autant) mais c’est surtout en regardant La La Land en 2016 que son amour pour cette industrie est né. Aujourd’hui, Drifa adore partager cette passion et ses connaissances à travers des articles, des quiz et des interviews et rencontres avec les actrices, acteurs et cinéastes comme Celine Song, Danny Boyle ou encore Tom Hardy et Timothée Chalamet, qu’elle admire.

title: After A Long Marriage, I Started Dating Again In My 50s. I Didn’t Expect The Reaction I Got From Much-Younger Men.
author: Hilary Rubin
body:
After my divorce settled, and following years spent raising my children and caring for my mother in her final chapter, I began to dip my toe back into the dating pool at 51.
Even though I felt ready to open up to the possibility of romance, I was also very aware of my emotional capacity ― what I had the bandwidth to hold and what I didn’t. I wasn’t looking for a soulmate, nor was I interested in future-tripping, making long-term promises or auditioning for a major role in a partner’s established life.
Before my marriage, my natural inclination had always been toward older men ― men with established footholds, refined perspectives and the gravitational pull of maturity. But after a long marriage and years of caregiving, my needs had shifted. I simply did not have the emotional reserve to play a significant role in a partner’s existing domestic ecosystem.
Given that, and at the behest of my curious married friends who urged me to “take one for the team,” I manually adjusted my age preferences on the apps, sliding the scale far enough left that it could be framed as a cultural statement. I widened those parameters not as a hunt but as an experiment in lowering the stakes. I assumed I was simply opening a doorway to casual conversation. What I didn’t expect was the immediate, enthusiastic response from men 10, 15 and 20 years my junior.
Unlike men in my own demographic, who often carried the weight of past domestic entanglements or rigid expectations, these younger suitors approached dating with refreshing candor, often addressing the age gap upfront with curiosity rather than hesitation, viewing it not as an obstacle but as a primary attraction.
I quickly realized this wasn’t an anomaly; I had stumbled onto a quiet, deliberate movement of young men actively seeking out older women.
Of course, it’s impossible to address this cultural wave without confronting the hyper-sexualized “cougar” or “MILF” tropes that are pervasive in the media. As a result, a not-insignificant portion of the messages in my inbox was inevitably fueled purely by a fantasy that reduced an older woman to an erotic milestone rather than a person. Distinguishing genuine intrigue from fetishization was the primary task of navigating this pool.
Still, a substantial segment of these younger men started surprisingly earnest conversations, and one young professional immediately stood out. He was 36 to my 51, but far more mature than his peers, intensely focused on his career, yet looking for adult female companionship.
What began as a series of engaging dinners turned into a meaningful, purposeful connection for both of us. For him, it offered a space to laugh, share and connect, entirely free from the biological clock and domestic pressure cooker of peer-group dating. For me, it served as a gentle, low-stakes step back into a dating landscape I hadn’t navigated in nearly two decades.
Our relationship spanned roughly 18 months ― a fluid, unhurried arrangement anchored in complete transparency, mutual discretion and shared pleasure, deliberately unburdened by demands for formal exclusivity or traditional milestones. We remain friends today, and while he still occasionally gives a quiet wink asking to return to that season, we mostly laugh about our time together.
Recently, on a getaway to an upscale Southern California suburb, I overheard a hotel concierge advising guests on a few local restaurants — playfully referred to as “cougar bars” — where younger men gather specifically in hopes of meeting women their senior. Who would have thought? What I quietly discovered on the fringes of dating app filters had spilled into everyday public life.
For generations, the older-man-younger-woman dynamic wasn’t just tolerated; it was the default social blueprint. When high-profile men married partners decades their junior, culture treated it as a standard perk of status and wealth. Society rarely questioned their motives or demanded they defend their choices.
Meanwhile, when the gender roles were reversed, we coined the term “cougar” to paint older women as predatory or desperate, and the younger men who dated them as novelties or “boy toys.” High-profile exceptions, like Demi Moore and Ashton Kutcher, were usually treated as tabloid anomalies or public spectacles.
Today, that archaic framework is fracturing, largely driven by the cold mechanics of modern dating technology. According to Pew Research, 63% of men under 30 report being single, compared to just 34% of women in the same age bracket. Furthermore, 64% of men report feeling insecure due to a staggering lack of incoming messages on apps. On platforms like Tinder, where the average match rate for men sits at a dismal 5%, young men face a brutal numbers game.
To survive the feed, younger men have learned to game the system. On Bumble and Hinge, a 26-year-old man has to manually slide his age preferences upward to appear in a 50-something or 60-something woman’s queue. Widening his age bracket may partly be a numerical calculation to expand his reach, but it is also a deliberate tactical shift. Rather than chasing low response rates among his peers, he may recognize that mature women operate with far greater clarity, efficiency and directness, making an interaction not only more statistically probable but also of higher baseline quality.
Bumble’s global data shows that nearly 60% of women are open to dating younger men. Meanwhile, Hinge Labs reports that 65% of young men want deep emotional intimacy early on, yet nearly half hold back, perhaps for fear of failing to meet the intense life-stage expectations of women their own age.
This brings us to the core of the dynamic. As The New York Times recently highlighted in its exploration of why younger men are seeking out mature women, featuring commentary from writer Emily Leibert and psychoanalyst Jamieson Webster, this phenomenon sits at the intersection of female liberation and male risk-aversion.
A mature, established woman may act as an oasis for a younger man, offering high-value connection, emotional composure and engaging conversation without demanding that he immediately step into the role of provider, husband or father.
In a culture where young men are overwhelmed by economic instability and shifting relationship expectations, seeking out an older woman may function as a shortcut to low-pressure connection. If she has her own financial stability, her own home and her own identity, she probably isn’t asking him to build a life with her. Her life is already built.
Yet that’s where the friction lies.
Some younger men are drawn to an older woman under the naive assumption that her self-sufficiency will make her “low maintenance.” Younger men may mistake an established woman’s independence for a lack of standards, assuming that because she doesn’t need his financial support or a traditional commitment, she requires minimal effort.
The reality, of course, is the exact opposite. True self-sufficiency comes with firm boundaries, high standards and zero tolerance for playing a supporting role in someone else’s unwritten script. An older woman who has raised children, built a career or cared for aging parents knows the exact value of her time and emotional investment.
Today, at 62, I look back on that chapter of my life with gratitude, but also with clarity. As a single woman now, my desires have shifted once again, and so has my capacity.
While I still open dating apps occasionally, mostly while traveling, my criteria have evolved. I’ve reopened my bracket to men in their early 50s and beyond, seeking the sharp, intellectually vibrant partners I’ve always aligned with best. I am no longer seeking the low-bandwidth, transitional space that post-divorce life required. Now I’m looking for someone ready for 30-plus years of shared curiosity and real depth.
While Kinsey Institute survey data shows that older women report higher levels of relationship satisfaction and commitment when dating younger men, I believe that satisfaction relies entirely on mutual transparency.

title: Ralph Lauren delivers modern take on romance with sensual silhouettes - Sentinel Colorado
author: BEATRICE DUPUY Associated Press
body:
The Ralph Lauren womenswear brand is a love letter to the designer’s wife of more than 60 years.
Ricky Lauren, his lifelong muse, is present in each of the designer’s collections.
At the designer’s New York Fashion Week show, Ricky Lauren sat front row along with other members of the Lauren family as her husband took guests on a whirlwind romantic escape ahead of the official launch of New York Fashion Week.
Actors Meghann Fahy, Cynthia Erivo, Viola Davis, Elizabeth Debicki and Ella Hunt were a few of the celebrity guests in attendance at the downtown Manhattan show.
“Ralph just generally designs so beautifully for a woman’s body,” Hunt told The Associated Press after the show.
Lauren pared down the lavish setting from his fall ready-to-wear show of opulent rugs and antique chairs, keeping the setting white and minimalist with attendees sitting on ivory fabric benches and models emerging from behind white doors.
Models glided down the rows of fashionable guests in soft and sensual silhouettes with a color palette of navy and white to the tunes of love songs, including “Every Little Thing She Does Is Magic” by The Police.
For Lauren, the collection was an “irreverent take on romance” that “upends traditional notions of chic.”
“It’s about ways of dressing that celebrate ingenuity, character, and originality — the freedom and fun of creating a style that is truly personal,” the designer said in his show notes.
Lauren opened the show with a white corseted top and white tailored pants before an array of deep, rich blues unfurled down the runway.
The 86-year-old designer played with his signature tailored designs incorporating billowing white pinstriped pants and dramatic floor-length overcoats.
Lauren accentuated his refined looks with touches of flair from oversized flowered brooches, feathered bolero jackets draped over evening gowns with plunging necklines to fringed scarves tied at the waist. While some models strutted in heels, others walked the runway in slipper-like flats. Either way, the models looked ready to jet off on a European getaway in their elegantly laid-back white pants and straw hats or pose on a red carpet in his evening gowns.
“What Ralph Lauren is doing this year is writing through his clothes about a very kind of modern dream,” David Lauren, the label’s chief branding and innovation officer, said.
